name: route_low_risk_named_fact_suggestion_goes_on_sheet_in_derived_block
spec_quote: A suggestion is never used on its own — low-risk questions included (Joey 2026-11-06): it goes on the sheet for his one-click confirm → `qa_add.py` → a rule for every job that asks it. / Derived-from-facts block on top: suggestions DeepSeek derived from a named fact (e.g. Preferred Last Name → Doe, from last_name) are listed together with their fact; Joey can accept the whole block with one click (still his confirm; each accepted item → qa_add.py).

name: route_jd_dependent_fact_suggestion_not_in_derived_block

input.question: Do you have at least 1 year professional work experience?

why: The spec says such a suggestion is 'listed one by one' but never says whether it still carries the one-click confirm on the sheet or must be answered by Joey himself. It is unambiguously excluded from the derived block, so 'sheet' with derived_block=false is the closest reading; 'joey' cannot be fully ruled out.
spec_quote: A fact whose meaning depends on the posting (answer_rules `jd: true`, today `yoe_meets` = "meets the JD's stated years") never makes a suggestion derived: e.g. "Do you have at least 1 year professional work experience?" → Yes from yoe_meets is listed one by one.

name: rank_greedy_marginal_value_with_tier_and_frequency_tiebreak
spec_quote: At most 20–30 questions per morning, ordered by marginal value: greedily, the question whose answer turns the most jobs fully ready (every remaining question answered) comes first — not raw frequency. / Tie-break when two questions would make the same number of jobs ready: the one more jobs ask comes first (tier A/B jobs counted before C/D), then the alphabetically smaller id.

name: stale_ok_job_read_two_days_ago_not_reread_under_three_day_recheck
spec_quote: New jobs daily; read jobs re-checked every few days; closed postings marked.
